readout_other: head-scratching count over 2 h by video; laser speckle contrast imaging of CBF in freely moving rats
direction_notes: Neural activity was not recorded; ultrasound given before (prevention) or after (therapy) nitroglycerin reduced head scratches versus untreated migraine rats and did not change the nitroglycerin-induced fall in CBF velocity.
safety_notes: Temperature rise from ultrasound was estimated by equation at about 8.2e-3 C; no in-vivo safety assessment described.

exposures.label: whole-brain TUS, prevention and therapy groups

target.label: the whole rat brain was stimulated by ultrasound and there were no specific brain targets

timing.protocol_description: Methods state 500 kHz, stimulation duration 400 ms, PRF 1 kHz and duty cycle 50%; the Fig. 1 legend and Discussion state SD 15 min, PRF 1 Hz and duty cycle 5%. TUS for 15 min given either before (Pre) or after (The) subcutaneous nitroglycerin; burst/pulse duration cannot be resolved.

source_quotes.n_subjects: In Group 3, seven rats underwent TUS for 15 min, followed by subcutaneous injection of nitroglycerin [TUS (Pre) group], and the ultrasound wave entered the brain tissue directly above the skull. In Group 4, seven rats were subcutaneously injected with nitroglycerin, followed by TUS for 15 min [TUS (The) group], and ultrasound waves entered the brain tissue from the side of the skull. In Group 5, seven rats used for preparing deafness models underwent TUS for 15 min, followed by subcutaneous injection of nitroglycerin [TUS (Pre)-Sham group-1]. In Group 6, seven rats used for preparing deafness models were subcutaneously injected with nitroglycerin, followed by TUS for 15 min [TUS (The)-Sham group-1]. Ultrasound waves were applied close to the ear but did not pass through the brain tissue in groups 5 and 6. In Group 7, five rats used for preparing deafness models underwent TUS for 15 min, followed by subcutaneous injection of nitroglycerin [TUS (Pre)-Sham group-2]. The stimulation mode of group 7 was the same as that of group 3. In Group 8, five rats used for preparing deafness models were subcutaneously injected with nitroglycerin, followed by TUS for 15 min [TUS (The)-Sham group-2].
